usage_desc: observes real-time incoming charged particles (plasma) in the solar wind, focusing on collecting pressure, temperature, and density parameters that directly impact Earth.
proton_density_desc: Number of particles per cubic centimeter (n/cc). Higher densities exert stronger dynamic pressure on Earth's magnetosphere.
bulk_speed_desc: Velocity of the plasma stream (km/s). Typical ambient solar wind ranges from 300 to 500 km/s, while Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) can accelerate speeds beyond 1,000 km/s.
ion_temp_desc: Thermal kinetic excitation of ions within the solar wind stream (Unit: Kelvin).
impacts_desc: When SWEPAM detects extreme spikes (e.g. speeds exceeding 600 km/s or elevated proton densities), it can trigger profound effects on terrestrial and orbital infrastructures:
satellites_desc: High-energy particles penetrate electronic payloads, inducing single-event upsets, GPS navigation degradation, and high-frequency (HF) radio blackouts.
power_grid_desc: Intense geomagnetic storms induce Geomagnetically Induced Currents (GIC) in high-voltage transmission lines, potentially causing transformer damage and large-scale power outages.
aurora_desc: Charged particle precipitation excites upper-atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen atoms, generating vibrant aurora displays at high and polar latitudes.
orbit_desc: L1 Sun-Earth Lagrangian Point (~1.5 million km sunward)
credits_intro: All real-time solar wind data and visual telemetry in this dashboard are publicly provided by international scientific institutions:
swpc_desc: Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC): Division of NOAA supplying operational real-time solar wind JSON telemetry streams.
nasa_desc: NASA ACE Project Science Office: Advanced Composition Explorer mission team managing spacecraft telemetry.
lanl_desc: Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL): Scientific instrument payload team for SWEPAM sensor calibration and data reduction.
api_note: Telemetry Stream: Pulled via NOAA SWPC JSON Services, updated every 1 minute.
